findings.description: PilotSubmission.derivative is always treated as optionally absent. No preparation branch makes it required when frame_indices is nonempty, validates the selected indices against the derivative, or establishes the attachment's media correspondence. Consequently, a submission with frame_indices=[0] and derivative=null produces a usable E3 context with no diagnostic. I reproduced that result using the actual preparation/reader functions in an isolated standard-library harness, supplied repository schemas, and equivalent schemas for the selected MediaAsset/Evidence fields. The existing pilot admission contract explicitly requires a derivative for frame attachments. This violates the sealed requirement that active dependent prerequisites be available before construction of a usable branch.

BindingContext replay checks a referenced FirstView's created_at against binding.first_view_at but never checks that the FirstView media/registration identify the binding's content. An unrelated, correctly pinned FirstView with the same timestamp can therefore supply usable chronology. Merely declaring and traversing FirstView.media and registration does not establish their relationship to this binding. The existing generation.validate_admission contract explicitly checks this content identity, so this is a lost prerequisite consistency check rather than a new policy request.

Chronology correspondence uses raw string equality. The boundary validates timestamps but returns their original strings. Existing Artifact timestamps may retain a non-UTC offset, while IntentBinding Instant fields normalize to UTC. Thus an admissible registration created_at of 2026-09-30T17:00:01-07:00 and registered_at of 2026-10-01T00:00:01Z are incorrectly rejected as a binding registration mismatch. Independently confirmed these strings represent the same instant. The FirstView comparison has the same problem.

The focused tests do not satisfy A2 oracle rule 4 or the sealed requirement to cover each new branch/adapter. For example, no negative case exercises binding registration mismatch, binding chronology time mismatch, binding seal intent mismatch, binding origin anchors mismatch, or run link context mismatch. Existing admitted fixtures exercise successful correspondence, while corruption cases target other conditions. Removing these rejection guards would not change those test expectations. The inventory test also proves only a small subset of declarations, and its uniqueness assertion checks a value already deduplicated by production code. The exhaustive A3 matrix does not excuse these missing A2 validator controls.
